title: COVID-19 Vaccination Status (Prevention of Discrimination) Bill 2022
short_title: COVID-19 Vaccination Status (Prevention of Discrimination) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit discrimination based on COVID-19 vaccination status by governments and other entities across employment, education, accommodation, sport and access to goods and services.
Its definition of discrimination would include demands for vaccination proof and unfavourable treatment linked to a person not having received a COVID-19 vaccination.

Exceptions would cover government-employed frontline health and care workers, while the prohibitions would override other Commonwealth, state or territory laws permitting vaccination-based discrimination.
changes: Children under 18 could receive a vaccination only with permission from a parent or guardian.
The prohibitions would extend to businesses and voluntary bodies.
A review would be required as soon as possible after the legislation had operated for 12 months.
summary.affected: Governments, employers, businesses, voluntary organisations, service users and families considering childhood vaccination would be affected.

divisions.question: Covid-19 Vaccination Status (Prevention of Discrimination) Bill 2022 - Second Reading - Put the question

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2024-08-14.10.1) to agree with the main idea of the bill, which means it passed. In parliamentary jargon, they voted against reading the bill for a second time. This was a private member's bill sponsored by Queensland Senator [Pauline Hanson](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/queensland/pauline_hanson) (One Nation). However, this question was [voted on for a second time](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/divisions/senate/2024-08-14/3) as several senators were on the wrong side of the room due to an error. ### What does the bill do? According to the [bill homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/s1358), the bill: > *Prohibits discrimination based on a person's COVID-19 vaccination status by the Commonwealth, state and territory governments, statutory authorities, local governments, and private enterprises.*
